The history of LEGO and video games can be divided into two sections. The first, starting with 1997's LEGO Island, was a tale of games in various genres using the generic LEGO brand in various ways. The second era focused on a particular brand of action-adventure mixing another license with LEGO's charms. This began 11 years ago with LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game.

LEGO Star Wars was developed by Traveller's Tales, a studio that has since made about 20 of these games total. But even before 2005, they were an experienced studio, having worked on all sorts of titles. They were probably best known for making Sonic R and Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex and Twinsanity.

The basis of the "LEGO license" game were mostly established in the first title. The game supported easy cooperative play, lacked a Game Over status, gave players a total of over 50 characters to control, was full of collectables, and provided a humorous interpretation of an otherwise disliked trilogy.

Oddly enough, the game was released a few weeks before Episode 3. Spoilers were had

The first LEGO Star Wars was a big hit, selling over 7 million copies worldwide. However, the true success ended up being the strong sales of future LEGO adaptations. The 2006 sequel sold about as well as the original, and 2007's compilation of the two games, The Complete Saga, sold more than the duo combined. The success of the formula extended beyond Star Wars. Marvel, Batman, Harry Potter, The Lord of the Rings, and Pirates of the Caribbean found success by mingling with LEGO. And seeing how last year's LEGO Jurassic World was another success, it seems like the series will continue for a while longer.
